content: 1. The efficacy of sodium picosulfate is reduced when colonic bacterial flora, necessary for its conversion to the active drug, is altered. This can occur due to co-administration with antibiotics. Close monitoring is required. 2. Fludrocortisone and sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid may increase each other's toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. This combination may lead to fluid and electrolyte imbalances, such as hypokalemia. 3. Flurbiprofen and sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid may increase each other's toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. Fluid and electrolyte imbalances may occur. 4. Fosfomycin reduces the effects of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Gemifloxacin reduces the effects of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering its metabolism. Additionally, sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid decreases gemifloxacin levels through cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Administer gemifloxacin at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid to avoid magnesium chelation. Monitor closely. 6.
